reason: The first reading was reread on the images with Mone and Waddell at hand, which restored 'letemur in perpetuum iuncti polorum atriis', confirmed 'tue corone' and the strophe order of Qui pressura, and established which pages belong to which leaf.
sources: F. J. Mone, Lateinische Hymnen des Mittelalters I (Freiburg 1853), nos. 84-91, pp. 112-116 (archive.org OCR text)
C. Waddell, The Primitive Cistercian Breviary (Fribourg 2007), pp. 432, 569, 586, 630 (Google Books snippets)
C. Blume, Thesauri hymnologici hymnarium (1908), p. 131 (snippet)
Cantus Index 008330, 008275.1, 008294; MMMO a03058 in Munich, BSB Clm 2541, f. 145v, and Heidelberg, Cod. Sal. X,7, f. 146r
text:
SOURCE-ASSISTED READING (stams-2026-10-30b), made with Mone, Lateinische Hymnen I nos. 84-91, and Waddell, The Primitive Cistercian Breviary (snippets), at hand. Reread on the native images by a research reader: canvas 0 left and right pages, all lines; canvas 1 right page, all lines. Canvas 1 left page was read on the image by an independent research reader. Expansions in ( ); [ ] lost, damaged or supplied; (?) uncertain; / line break. Neumes not transcribed.

Images: https://fragmentarium.ms/loris/F-x6cz/Stams_STA_Frg_134_01r.jpg (canvas 0) and https://fragmentarium.ms/loris/F-x6cz/Stams_STA_Frg_134_01v.jpg (canvas 1), each 7360 x 4912. Regions x,y,width,height in native pixels. Leaf A = canvas 0 right (recto) + canvas 1 left (verso); leaf B = canvas 1 right (recto) + canvas 0 left (verso).

Leaf A recto, canvas 0 right page, region 4300,1000,2050,2750 (line 1 also 4350,1080,1950,250):
con[...] (abraded) [l]etemur in perpetuum iu(n)cti polo /
[rum a]triis. [red G]loria tibi d(omi)ne. [red] De virginib(us). /
[red I]esu corona virginu(m) que(m) mater [illa] (hole) /
concepit que sola virgo parturit hec vo /
ta clemens accipe. [red Q]ui pascis inter /
lilia septus choreis virginu(m) spons(as) decor(ans) /
gloria sponsisq(ue) reddens premia. [red] ymnus (partly in a hole) /
[red flourished Q]uocu(m)q(ue) pergis virgines sequuntur

Leaf A verso, canvas 1 left page, region 1750,1150,2050,2650 (independent reader):
adque laudibus post te canentes cur[si] /
tant ymnosq(ue) dulces personant. [red T]e /
[de]precamur largius nostris adauge /
mentib(us) nescire prors(us) omnia corrupti /
onis vulnera. [red G]loria tibi. [red] In dedicatione /
[red X]p(ist)e cunctorum dominator alme /
patris eterni genitus ab ore supplicum /
vota pariterq(ue) ymnu(m) cerne benignus.
(A second, lighter layer of small stemmed notes stands beside the rhombic notes over lines 6-7.)

Leaf B recto, canvas 1 right page, region 4150,1150,2300,2650:
[...]lis beata nobis gaudia. [red G]loria tibi domine /
gloria unigenito una cu(m) s(an)c(t)o sp(irit)u in sempiterna s(e)c(u)la am(en). /
[red B]eata [erased word] xp(ist)i passio sit nostra libe- [margin, red, region 5900,1850,600,300: "ad" + con-sign(?) + "p" + tall letter with hook; ad (com)pl(etorium)? or ad pri(mam)?, not read with confidence] /
ratio ut per hanc nobis gaudia sint parata ce /
lestia. [red Q]ui pressura mortis dura solvisti nex /
us criminum nos ad pacem duc veracem ihesu /
corona virginum. [red I]n amara crucis ara fu /
disti rivos sanguinis ihesu digne rex benigne

Leaf B verso, canvas 0 left page, region 1850,1000,2050,2750:
consors paterni luminis. [red S]anguis xp(ist)i [qui] fu[isti] (end damaged) /
peremptor hostis invidi fac sitire da venire ad /
cenam agni providi. [red T]ue genti recolenti tue co /
rone(?) supplicium da virtutem et salutem xp(ist)e /
redemptor omnium. [red L]aus honor virtus gloria /
deo patri et filio sancto simul paraclyto in sem /
piterna secula amen. [red] ad t(er)ciam ymnus /
[large red I]esu velatus facie fuisti sol iusticie flexis illu-
